{{Otheruses|mother|more=father (disambiguation)}}
{{Cleanup|[[WP:MOS]]}}
{{Quote|My dad loves me very much.''"<br />"''True, and when you become a father, you'll discover how true that is.|[[Ben Skywalker|Ben]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Conviction">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]''</ref>}}
[[File:3rodians.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] parents with their offspring]]
A '''parent''' was the progenitor of biological offspring. Some [[Species/Legends|species]], such as [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorths]], had only one, asexually [[Reproduction/Legends|reproducing]] parent. Most species, however, reproduced sexually: a [[Gender/Legends|male]] or female parent was called a '''father''' or a '''mother''', respectively. ''Parent'' also referred to a caretaker of the offspring. In many societies across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the biological parents were responsible for raising their young; however, this varied from species to species, and between different cultures. Sometimes, a child, or [[Youngling/Legends|youngling]], would be raised by their grandparents or other family members. Some parents, such as adoptive parents, were not biologically related to their children at all.

==Biological parent==
[[File:Lukemaraben.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Human parents [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] with their newborn son, [[Ben Skywalker|Ben]]]]
{{Quote|Now I have something wonderful, something I have chosen. And I will never let anyone take the child I'm carrying.|From the private journal of [[Etain Tur-Mukan]]|<ref name="Triple Zero">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref>}}
One of the important criteria that formed a universal definition of "life" was [[Reproduction/Legends|reproduction]]: living organisms create more living organisms.<ref name="GG4-2">[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'', Second Edition]]</ref> Some people believed that the very purpose of life was to create new life, and that creating life was the greatest act a living creature could commit.<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>

===One progenitor===
{{Quote|You are a clone. That means you are my son. Period. No one else, no woman was involved.|[[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], to his son, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba]]|<ref name="Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive">''[[Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive]]''</ref>}}
Some species had only one progenitor. Most [[Gastropod/Legends|gastropods]], for example, reproduced asexually,<ref name="NEGAS" /> and [[Plant/Legends|plant]]-based species reproduced themselves.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Notable examples were:
*[[Assembler]]s, an [[Spider/Legends|arachnid]] species which created drones to carry out day-to-day affairs. These drones, called nodes, were created from the essence of the Assembler's web, and were both part of the Assembler and separate from them. New Assemblers evolved from these nodes.<ref name="Essential">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>
*The [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorth]], or space slug, reproduced through fission, in which the slug split in two smaller slugs.<ref>[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]; ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' says that space slugs would carry the young for a few [[Standard month/Legends|months]], and then give birth</ref>
*[[Filordus|Filordi]] reproduced asexually while [[Death/Legends|dying]]. A week after its "parent" has died, an infant Filordus crawls from the corpse of its predecessor.<ref name="Ultimate">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref>
*[[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] were a hermaphroditic species whose members possessed multiple types of reproductive organs simultaneously.<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> They needed no partner to produce a child.<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars novelization">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' novelization]]</ref> However, some Hutts did have both a mother and a father; one example was [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Ziro]] the Hutt<ref name="HuntForZiro">{{TCW|Hunt for Ziro}}</ref> and [[Gorga's son|the son]] of [[Anachro]] and [[Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo/Legends|Gorga]] the Hutt.<ref name="BoBFMurder">''[[Boba Fett: Murder Most Foul]]''</ref>
*The [[Neti/Legends|Neti]] were a plant-based species who, like most plants, procreated by producing a few seeds.<ref name="Essential" />
*The [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]] [[Sarlacc/Legends|sarlacc]] reproduced via plantlike spores, although very few took root.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Some species were fully '''parthenogenetic'''&mdash;that is, every member of the species was female and reproduced without fertilization. Theoretically, the offspring should therefore be genetically identical to its mother, which was the nature of '''parthenogenesis'''.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> [[M'shinn]] were a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species in which every individual was female, who reproduced through a form of parthenogenesis. In areas where their food was plentiful, a M'shinn would give birth to a single infant once every three [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]]. All M'shinni looked almost identical, although each generation's genetic code was subtly altered.<ref name="GG12">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref> The [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Sekct]] were fully parthenogenetic. Every individual would lay a single egg every two years, from which a single infant hatched. The genetic code of the Sekct were very susceptible to change, and random mutations ensured that each offspring was different from its parent.<ref name="Alien Encounters">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref>

[[File:BobaJango-CVD.png|thumb|right|180px|Jango Fett with his clone son, Boba]]
[[Cloning/Legends|Cloning]] was the process of reproducing a near symmetrical duplicate of a being through artificial means. [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba]] was created by [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] as an unaltered clone, at the request of his "father," the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]].<ref name="Episode 2">{{Film|II}}</ref> Boba was raised as Jango's offspring, and his father always put his son first&mdash;like any father should, according to Boba.<ref name="Bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Vianna D'Pow]], a [[Zeltron/Legends|Zeltron]] [[Albino/Legends|albino]] bounty hunter, placed an order for a solitary clone of herself from Kaminoan cloners.<ref name="One of a Kind">{{CWACite|8|One of a Kind (comic story)}}</ref>

===Two progenitors===
{{Quote|Something wonderful has happened.|[[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] tells [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|her husband]] that she's pregnant|<ref name="Episode 3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
Many [[Species/Legends|species]] had members of female and male sexes who reproduced sexually between two respective individuals.

For some, the process of creating a new organism involved the fusion of cells from each parent;<ref name="Isard's">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref> examples were [[Bith/Legends|Bith]],<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]]<ref name="Isard's" /> and [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="Isard's" /> Many species reproduced by laying [[Egg/Legends|eggs]]. For some of them, sera from one parent fertilized the egg created by another parent. Reptilians, for example, reproduced by laying fertilized eggs<ref name="NEGAS" /> (although the [[Sekct]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Marca/Legends|Marca]] reproduced without fertilization<ref name="Alien Encounters" />). Other notable examples were the [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibious]] [[Ishi Tib/Legends|Ishi Tib]]<ref name="NEGAS" /> and [[Issori]],<ref name="Isard's" /> and the [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]].<ref name="GG4-1">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref>

Some species were genderless, but two individuals were still required in order to create offspring. Notable examples included:
*[[Aganof]], who were androgynous. They had both male and female characteristics and laid fertilized eggs after mating.<ref name="Alien Encounters" />
*The plant-like [[Ergesh]] were asexual beings and had no concept of gender. They reproduced by a species ritual in which two Ergesh each produced a seed that was then planted together in a [[Shoolbloorp|swamp]]. Over time, the seeds would combine and a new individual would emerge.<ref name="Alien Encounters" />
*[[Protean]]s were [[Silicon/Legends|silicon]]-based life forms. Even though they were genderless, they still paired off to reproduce. Two Proteans would merge into a single entity, which would eventually crack open, revealing the original Protean pair and a newborn.<ref name="Alien Encounters" />
*Verpine were insectoid hermaphrodites. When an increase in population was needed, some individuals produced the eggs, while others provided the necessary sera.<ref name="GG4-1" />

Members of different species were usually incapable of producing viable offspring,<ref name="GG4-2" /> although exceptions did exist. An individual with parentage from more than one sentient species was known as a [[Hybrid/Legends|hybrid]]. Humans, for example, were able to interbreed with [[Near-Human]]s with few exceptions<ref name="NEGAS" /> and could also interbreed with the [[Coynite/Legends|Coynite]],<ref name="Uhl Eharl">{{JournalCite|8|Uhl Eharl Khoehng (short story)}}</ref> [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]]<ref name="Twileks">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''; however, according to ''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]'' and ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]'', Humans and Twi'leks were genetically incompatible.</ref> [[Kalai]]<ref name="Zirtrans">{{JournalCite|5|Zirtran's Anchor (article)}}</ref> and [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]].<ref name="OREncyc">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Other compatible hybrid combinations included [[Borneck]] with [[Etti]],<ref name="Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals">{{InsiderCite|66|Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals}}</ref> and [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] with [[Sephi/Legends|Sephi]].<ref name="KotOR48">[[Knights of the Old Republic 48|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 48]]</ref> Bothans were able to interbreed with at least one species, resulting in the so-called [[half-Bothan]]s.<ref name="EGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Some species could interbreed only with the help of genetic manipulation; Humans could interbreed with [[Anzat (species)|Anzati]], [[Qiraash/Legends|Qiraash]], [[Rattataki/Legends|Rattataki]] and [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbarans]] this way.<ref name="CN2">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> Many species ostracized members who bore hybrid children.<ref name="Nightlily">{{StoryCite|story=Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>

===Others===
The [[Shard (species)|Shards]] of [[Orax]] were a unique life form. These silicone-based sentient crystals did not reproduce and had no progenitors in the common sense of the word. They formed from an interaction between the ion-charged [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and the natural crystals and [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]]-rich [[Water/Legends|water]], "growing" Shards in clusters. When a Shard had reach full size and "adulthood," the accretion of crystal would begin to produce a new Shard.<ref name="Alien Encounters Shard">{{JournalCite|15|Alien Encounters (article series)|Alien Encounters: The Shard}}</ref><ref name="Alien Encounters" />

The [[Bartokk]] were a mysterious insectoid species with exceptional regenerative abilities. If their brain was cut in half, each half would regenerate into a separate twin, creating an entirely new individual.<ref name="Ultimate" />

==Adoption==
[[File:BailBrehaLeia-hd.png|thumb|right|270px|Bail and Breha Organa with their newly adopted daughter]]
{{Quote|I was accepted as their child everywhere we went. I almost forgot where I was from, until I looked in the mirror.|[[Rush Clovis/Legends|Rush Clovis]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] who was adopted by a [[Muun/Legends|Muun]] when he was twelve|<ref name="The Rise of Clovis">{{TCW|The Rise of Clovis}}</ref>}}
'''Adoption''' was a process where a person assumed the parenting for another. An '''adoptive parent''' was one who nurtured and raised the offspring of the biological parents but may not have been related to the youngling.

The process varied from planet to planet, and between different cultures. On the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], people who wanted to adopt had to fill in an application and several datafiles, and gather "all the other stuff" that the official would want before the adoption took place.<ref name="Isard's" /> Among the Mandalorians, on the other hand, the process was rather simple. In a ritual known as the ''[[gai bal manda]]'' ("name and soul"), a prospective Mandalorian parent needed only to recite the phrase ''ni kyr'tayl gai sa'ad'' ("I know your name as my child") followed by the name of the individual to be adopted.<ref name="Culture">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>

Humans (and presumably many other species) viewed adoption as charitable.<ref name="Isard's" /> Some people chose to become adoptive parents because they could not have any children of their own; for example, [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail]] and [[Breha Organa/Legends|Breha Organa]] had many difficulties in producing an heir, and [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]] had informed them that another attempt to conceive a child would probably kill Breha.<ref name="Republic61">[[Republic 61|''Republic'' 61]]</ref> This led to discussions about adopting a baby girl, and the adoption of their daughter [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]].<ref name="Episode 3" /> Sometimes, a stepparent would adopt a stepchild.<ref name="Battlefronts">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]''</ref>

On the planet [[Gand (planet)/Legends|Gand]], the so-called [[Findsman/Legends|Findsmen]] of [[Gand/Legends|the species]] would sometimes find a child for couples who could not conceive. The Findsmen would wander into the enshrouding mists of the planet and find the child they desired. These "mistborn" children were a gift and raised by the people as their own.<ref name="I, Jedi" />

Adoption was extremely common in Mandalorian culture, even adoption of adults.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> As a warrior-people, Mandalorians had a savage reputation, but they cherished family life. Adoption of war orphans was quite common, even children of a defeated enemy, whereas other species might kill them. The Mandalorian way of life was a dangerous one, and Mandalorian families never hesitated to adopt orphans.<ref name="Culture" /> Despite the importance placed on fidelity and chastity prior to marriage,<ref name="Culture" /> a partner who acted unfaithfully during a long separation would be forgiven so long as any child that resulted from the indiscretion was raised together by the couple.<ref name="Triple Zero" /> Adoption could even be done posthumously.<ref name="O66" />

Some species had no need for adoption. A notable example was the Issori species. On their homeworld [[Issor]], the conception of a new child was something that was negotiated between families, and not connected to romantic love at all. Families would agree on breedings (a process in which eggs which were fertilized by an agent packet), and the families would raise the children. Therefore, they had no unwanted children, and even those who were orphaned were the responsibility of the families of those who were bred to create them.<ref name="Isard's" />

==Step-parent==
[[File:Suufamily.png|thumb|left|200px|Cut Lawquane with his wife and step-children, [[Jek Lawquane/Legends|Jek]] and [[Shaeeah Lawquane/Legends|Shaeeah]]]]
{{Quote|She took you and your sister as her own, straight away. She cared for you both ''so much'', Finn, and you instantly bonded with her. She'd lost so much as a slave. She hadn't thought she'd ever have her own life, let alone a life that included something as special as you two. You were everything.|[[Caled Galfridian]] tells the story about [[Nina Galfridian|his wife]] to his son, [[Finn Galfridian|Finn]]|<ref name="Invasian Rescues 4" />}}
A '''stepmother''' or '''stepfather''' was the [[Marriage/Legends|spouse]] of one's biological parent and not one's natural mother of father. If the other biological parent was deceased or had moved out of their children's life, the stepparent would often take their place as the second parent to the children; examples of this included [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker Lars]] and her [[Lars family/Legends|new family]] after she married [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]],<ref name="Episode 2 novel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref> [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] deserter [[Cut Lawquane/Legends|Cut Lawquane]], who married [[Suu Lawquane/Legends|Suu Lawquane]] and adopted her two children, [[Jek Lawquane/Legends|Jek Lawquane]] and [[Shaeeah Lawquane/Legends|Shaeeah Lawquane]];<ref name="Battlefronts" /> and [[Nina Galfridian]] and [[Galfridian family|her family]].<ref name="Invasian Rescues 4">[[Invasion: Rescues 4|''Invasion: Rescues'' 4]]</ref>

==Hold-parent==
A '''hold-parent''' was a close friend of a youngling's parents and an honorary title. Hold-parents would often bring gifts and toys to the child. In extreme circumstances, a hold-parent might assume the parenting of the youngling if something happened to the parents.<ref name="Crystal Star">''[[The Crystal Star]]''</ref>

==Grandparent==
{{Dialogue|Leia|Not ready to become a grandmother yet?|Mara|I think I'd throw myself on my lightsaber first.|Leia|I think I'm ready. I plan to be the sort of feisty, bad-example grandmother who teaches her grandchildren deplorable habits. ''[To Jacen]'' How long should I expect to wait?|Jacen|If you're trying to embarrass me, you're talking into a dead comlink.|Leia|Not embarrass. I'm just trying to get a timetable.|Jacen|Ask Jaina.|Leia|She said to ask you.|attr=[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] having a relaxed conversation with [[Darth Caedus|her son]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker|her sister-in-law]]|src=<ref name="LotFB">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref>}}
'''Grandparents''' were the parents of a person's own parent, whether that be a father or a mother. One could also be a '''step-grandparent'''.<ref name="I, Jedi" /> A female grandparent was called a '''grandmother''' and a male grandparent a '''grandfather'''. [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']], the Mandalorian language, was gender-neutral, so "grandmother" and "grandfather" were the same word in that language.<ref name="LotFR">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>

==Norms and customs==
[[File:TwilekMotherAndChild.png|thumb|right|230px|right|A [[Unidentified Twi'lek (mother)/Legends|Twi'lek mother]] with [[Unidentified Twi'lek child (hostage)/Legends|her child]]]]{{Quote|This is a happy moment. The happiest moment of my life.|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] upon hearing about [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|his wife's]] pregnancy|<ref name="Episode 3" />}}
The norms and customs concerning reproduction and parenting varied greatly between species, and sometimes within different cultures of a species. The [[Horansi]], for example, comprised several sub-species. Though they could cross-breed, these occurrences were rare, primarily due to cultural differences.<ref name="Alien Encounters" />

===Valuing children===
{{Quote|There are two truths... in my life. I loved your father and... whatever you may think... however it seems... I love you.|[[Morrigan Corde]] to [[Cade Skywalker|her son]]|<ref name="LW3">[[Legacy — War 3|''Legacy — War'' 3]]</ref>}}
The way parents valued their offspring varied between species as well. Among the [[Ebranite]], for instance, children were seen as little more than [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], and had very little freedom.<ref name="GG12" /> [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] young were raised in communal hives from birth, where they had only limited amounts of food. Many died as a result.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The [[Ortolan/Legends|Ortolans]] had few children. Education of the offspring was the responsibility of the parents, who pass their knowledge and skills they learned from their parents on to their children. When a child showed extraordinary aptitude in skills that are beyond the parents' expertise, they asked another Ortolan family to teach the child in return for some other service. However, parental obligations ended when the child reaches an age equivalent to seven years old, at which time they are simply thrown out of the house to forage on their own<ref name="GG4-1" /> and fend for themselves.<ref name="NEGAS" /> This is done in order to conserve the family's supplies, although exceptions are sometimes granted for children with a talent particularly valuable to the family's well-being.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] cared for their children, but they were not considered people until they had endured a ceremony that declared their adulthood. Babies often perished because of the harsh desert life, and Tusken Raiders took great pride knowing that only the strongest survived.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[File:Tyrellfam.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The [[Tyerell family]]. [[Aleena/Legends|Aleena]] were fiercely devoted to their families, and would often travel as a unit when they left [[Aleen/Legends|their homeworld]].<ref name="NEGAS" />]]
However, there were many species where parents were expected to love their children and be their teachers and protectors. The planet [[Cona/Legends|Cona]], for instance, was a dangerous place for the immature and uninitiated, and the [[Arcona/Legends|Arcona]] society arose from the need to ensure the safety of the young. Arcona parents would look after their hatchlings until they had learned the ways of the jungles of their homeworld. Because hatching a brood was a long-term commitment, Arcona did not form parental partnerships lightly.<ref name="GG4-1" />

Children formed the center of the [[Chadra-Fan/Legends|Chadra-Fan]] community;<ref name="GG4-1" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> they were adored, and cared for by all.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Everyone shared the duty of parenting one another's children, and households were open to anyone at all times.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Members of this quick-witted rodent species lived together in large clans, and children left their clan only to marry. The married couple resides with and bears children for the clan that currently has the fewest infants.<ref name="GG4-1" /> [[Yarkora/Legends|Yarkoran]] children were few and far between, and every child was doted upon and treated as a firstborn.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Kubaz/Legends|Kubaz]] also loved to dote on their families.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Dug/Legends|Dugs]] were extremely loyal to their family and would protect them and their children with passionate violence if they were insulted or attacked.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Although [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]] took great pleasure in slaughter and violence, they were also loving towards their children and mates.<ref name="NEGAS" />

The [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] and the [[Talz/Legends|Talz]] did not send their younglings to [[school]]; instead, the family units ''were'' the school. The Shistavanen were home-schooled using a government-approved system. The Talz had no formal schools, and most children were home-taught via cooperative family tutelage. Mothers and fathers who stood out in certain subjects would partner with those who excelled in others, so that their offspring would receive as well-rounded an education as possible.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[File:Anakinandmom.jpg|thumb|right|290px|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] bids farewell to [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|his mother]].]]The [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]] would pass down vocations&mdash;so-called "[[Blood/Legends|blood]] professions"&mdash;from generation to generation within each family, teaching the children the necessary skills to mine or be a mechanic.<ref name="NEGAS" />

===Relationships between parents===
{{Quote|You're not married&mdash;and you had a baby! You guys are gonna be in so much trouble!|A gleeful [[Ben Skywalker]] to [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] and [[Tenel Ka Djo|Tenel Ka]]|<ref name="DN2">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref>}}
The act of conceiving a child was typically connected with love and emotional attachments between the parents; this was a common notion among many of the species who reproduced sexually.<ref name="Isard's" /> Among the [[Gotal/Legends|Gotals]], love at first sight was the rule rather than the exception, because Gotals could read each other so well with their unique head cones. Relationships built on love would usually last. They mated for life and would bear children as soon as their lifestyle permitted.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Gotals took great delight in the raising of progeny, and their cone sensitivity enabled them to function well as a spouse and parent.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] couples would begin having children soon after marriage.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Some Humans viewed sex as forbidden unless sanctioned by marriage;<ref name="I, Jedi" /> Boba Fett, for example, believed that sex between those not married was immoral.<ref name="Last One Standing">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> Having a child out of wedlock was considered scandalous by some Humans.<ref name="DN2" /> The Arcona regarded a commitment to marry as a commitment to parent,<ref name="NEGAS" /> whereas the [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolans]] would mate for life and saw a happy mating, or marriage, as a necessary requirement for existence.<ref name="NEGAS" />

This was in stark contrast to species like the [[Goroth Prime/Legends|Goroth]],<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> who had no concept of marriage at all. There were many species, like the Ishi Tib of [[Tibrin/Legends|Tibrin]],<ref name="GG4-1" /> who would never marry and took no wife or husband.

Amongst some species, the concept of romantic love did not factor into reproduction and the raising of children. For the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]], reproduction was entirely a matter of rational selection.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Prospective parents took a sample of their [[DNA/Legends|DNA]] to a [[Computer Mating Service]] (CMS), which matched it with other samples.<ref name="GG4-1" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> From these comparisons, CMS developed a series of [[Computer/Legends|computer]] models projecting the outcome of a union between the customer and a dozen suitable mates.<ref name="GG4-1" /> A prospective parent ranked each combination according to their preferences, and a meeting was arranged between clients who selected the same combinations in approximately the same order. The prospective parents or their agents would negotiate the number of offspring and how many each parent would receive. Upon arriving at an agreement, the parents would send the necessary cells to a so-called Reproduction Center,<ref name="GG4-1" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> [[File:Fett_happy_family.png|thumb|left|210px|Boba Fett posing with [[Sintas Vel|his wife]] and [[Ailyn Vel|child]]. Many families liked to record family [[Hologram/Legends|holoimages]] of themselves.]]where the genetic material was combined, fertilized, and incubated.<ref name="GG4-1" /> After a year, the children were delivered to the parents' door. As they had reproduced in this manner for so long, Bith lost the ability to conceive naturally,<ref name="GG4-1" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> because the organs necessary to reproduce organically had atrophied past the point of being able to function in procreation.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Amongst the Issori, breedings were negotiated between families, and the female Issori laid eggs which were fertilized by an agent packet produced by a male. The children were raised by the families they were born into. Sometimes, eggs or packets from dead heroes or leaders were used in order to preserve the bloodline; the families always cared for these newborns.<ref name="Isard's" />

Among the [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]], who worshiped Nature, reproduction was blessed only if the church carried it out. Ho'Din would mate for life. A priestess "gathers" the "seed" of life from the male, distributing it to the female in imitation of the manner insects play a part in the reproduction of plants. Children born without the sanction of the church were drugged into sleep and killed, sacrificed to the forest floor where Nature could purify their soul. (Ho'Din parents rarely made such sacrifices, however, since the species were masters of herbal '''[[birth control]]''').<ref name="GG4-1" />

Many species and cultures, like the [[Besalisk/Legends|Besalisk]] and the [[Caamasi/Legends|Caamasi]],<ref name="NEGAS" /> placed great importance on monogamous relationships, although there were others species which did quite the opposite. For example:<br />
*Among the [[Cerean/Legends|Cereans]], females made up the majority of the population, with an average ratio of twenty to one. Therefore, polygamy was inevitable, with each male taking one "bond-wife" and several other "honor-wives."<ref name="NEGAS" />
*The ideas of marriage and monogamous relationships were unheard of in the Goroth culture. Goroth interbred within their clans, and to breed with a member of another clan brought great shame on the individuals and both clans.<ref name="Alien Encounters" />
*The [[Gorvan Horansi]], a sub-species of the Horansi species, were polygamous, and a tribe was composed of one male, all of his wives and all of their children.<ref name="Alien Encounters" />
*The [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] were a polygamous people where each male had multiple wives and many children.<ref name="NEGAS" />
*The insectoid [[Noehon]]s had a culture in which an alpha male controlled a "harem" of 10 to 50 females.<ref name="GG12" />
*A [[Ranat/Legends|Ranat]] female would come into "season" at least twice a year. During that time, she would mate with as many male Ranats as possible.<ref name="GG4-1" />
*A [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] core-family, or "warren-clan," was headed by one female, who would have children with several husbands.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Some species had two progenitors, but the resulting offspring was raised by one parent only. Among the [[Mashi Horansi]], the males would raise their young. The [[Treka Horansi]], on the other hand, shared a rough equality in regards to responsibility for their young.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> When Arcona reproduced, the males usually raised the children, as females were considered more reckless and irresponsible.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]] had vastly different personalities, and while the females would live their lives in comfortable homes and raise their young in villages, the males were driven by irresponsible wanderlust and preferred to live as vagrants. This kept males and females nearly constantly separated.<ref name="GG4-1" /> After choosing a mate and siring children, male Devaronians typically took to the rivers and roads of [[Devaron/Legends|their homeworld]], and many left the planet entirely, rarely ever returning. However, the males would always send some of the [[Currency/Legends|money]] they earned back home to their wives and children. The females preferred financial support over having the males present.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[File:VentressMother-Nightsisters.png|thumb|right|205px|A [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] [[Asajj Ventress's mother/Legends|mother]] with her infant daughter, [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]]]]
Among some species and cultures, the male was killed by the female after mating. Among the insectoid [[Flakax]] species, one singular female ruled each community and produced all of its young. The sole job of the males was to aid in reproduction, and after they had served their purpose, they were eaten by the female.<ref name="GG4-1" /> In the traditional [[H'nemthe (species)/Legends|H'nemthe]] mating ritual, the female disembowels the male with her razor-sharp tongue. The male considered the ritual a culmination of spiritual fulfillment, as he moves on to the netherworld to guide his coming child.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] were a culture of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] witches. After mating, the child's father was killed by tradition.<ref >''[[Star Wars: Infinity's End]]''</ref><ref >[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']], chapter 15: ''Quantum Being''</ref>

Many species, like [[Chagrian/Legends|Chagrians]],<ref name="NEGAS" /> Humans<ref name="NEGAS" /> and [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshans]]<ref name="NEGAS" /> would normally raise their children in private home groupings, usually the child's parents or family (or both, like the Kel Dor and the Shistavanens<ref name="NEGAS" />). Another example was the [[Xi'Dec/Legends|Xi'Dec]], a unique species of more than 180 sexes, where family units lived apart from other family units while caring for their children within the confines of the family.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Kubaz couples shared their apartment with their infants, but children went to live in a family crèche when they were still very young, the equivalent of five standard years. At the crèche, they were cared for by single adult pressures.<ref name="GG4-1" />

Among some species, raising and caring for the young was a task performed by a group of individuals. The amphibious [[Multopo]]s lived in tribes, whose primary function was to raise more Multopos. They spent a great deal of time caring for the eggs and the young together, and several adult Multopos would watch the water canals that served as "nurseries."<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> Among the [[Brubb]], the parents went their separate ways after their egg hatched, and the hatchling became a ward of the ''haba'', a group of 10 to 10,000 couples. Every youngling was considered property of the haba, and every adult took responsibility for rearing each child.<ref name="GG4-1" /> A Ranat female moved her children into a nursery after giving birth to them. There, she and the other mothers would take turns providing minimal care to all the children of the tribe. If the mother died, her children would not miss her, as they did not know her from the other nursemaids.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Among the Ishi Tib, the responsibility for raising the young fell to the community as a whole, and no one ever knew which child came from which parents.<ref name="GG4-1" />

The [[Rybet/Legends|Rybet]] were [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] nomads who only interacted with others of their kind to mate. [[Xenobiologist/Legends|Xenobiologists]] estimated that fewer than a billion Rybet existed in the galaxy, possibly due to the pathological hatred male Rybet had for female Rybet and vice versa. Only an overwhelming compulsion to reproduce could overcome the males' fear and loathing of Rybet females. Rybet felt a drive to reproduce only once every ten years after reaching adulthood. The only time when a male and female Rybet lived together for any length of time were in the first years of raising their young. For the first year or two, the parents would stay together, slaving their [[Starship/Legends|starships]] together and taking their parts in raising the young. This arrangement wouldn't last long, however; eventually, they would grate on each other's nerves, and after one or two years, the male either left or would find himself dead or severely maimed. The mother would typically sell the dead male's ship and give the young the resulting credits as start-up money.<ref name="Ultimate" />

[[File:Nyna_holo.jpg|thumb|left|230px|[[Morrigan Corde|Nyna Calixte]], a.k.a. Morrigan Corde, stares at her family holo.]]
For Brubb females, the process of bringing new life into the world was very stressful. Because of this, they usually died at a younger age than males (in order to prolong their lives, an increasing number of females refused to lay eggs). Because of the toll that process took on their bodies, a Brubb female would lay only a single egg each [[Baros]]ian year (567 [[Standard day/Legends|days]]). The female would select her mate with great care before the mating process. After mating, the male and female would usually protect the nest together. Sometimes, a male would mate with more than one female, which resulted in some females being forced to protect the egg all by themselves. Having to guard an egg alone bore such a stigma of disgrace that it was often considered a legitimate excuse for the female to murder the philandering male.<ref name="GG4-1" />

Some species and cultures would mate only once, for life; to the [[Cathar/Legends|Cathar]], the custom was so important that when one mate died, the survivor never had a relationship with another.<ref name="Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Redemption">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Redemption]]''</ref> The Mashi Horansi,<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> a Horansi sub-species,<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> were another notable example.

===Other customs===
{{Quote|You could have had children via a donor. Clinics can do clever things."<br />"''Mando'ade'' adopt. I chose the finest family a man could have. Why would we have wanted to conceive a child by donor?|[[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Bardan Jusik|Gotab]]|<ref name="LotFR" />}}
To some species, creating offspring was a duty. The concept of furthering one's family was extremely important to the [[Sludir]] of [[Sluudren]]. To die without an heir was considered disgraceful, and to deprive a family of an heir was grounds for banishment or execution.<ref name="GG12" /> A female Yarkora could only bear children every fifteen standard years, and usually only one at the time, making their species very sparse. Every female had to become a mother at some point in her life in order to save the species from extinction.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[File:Revan_and_T3-M4_TERC.jpg|thumb|right|280px|[[Revan/Legends|Revan]] watches a [[Holorecorder/Legends|holorecording]] of [[Bastila Shan|his wife]] and [[Vaner Shan|son]].]]
Some species had rather unusual customs when it came to parenting: When the [[Lahsbee/Huhk|Huhks]] produced offspring, they left their young&mdash;the Lahsbees&mdash;with the other Lahsbees. The Huhks and the Lahsbees could not understand each other's languages, and the Huhks did not appear to feel any particular need to protect the Lahsbees. In fact, they found them annoying in the extreme.<ref name="AA">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

Sometimes, the number of children an individual was allowed to have, or whether they were allowed to have offspring at all, was regulated by local laws. The planet [[Algara II]] was home to the native [[Xan/Legends|Xan]] and immigrated Humans. The Humans settlers were in complete control of the planet, and the Xan were second-class citizens. As a result, the Human Algarians strictly regulated the number of children the Xan were allowed to have.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> The Kaminoans controlled their genetic codes through cloning and selective breeding. As such, they were one of the most genetically homogeneous species in the galaxy, while the children were made within a set of strict, predetermined genetic parameters.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Green eyes, for example, were not allowed, only gray, yellow and blue. There was no room for any other [[Color/Legends|color]], and children born with another eye color were killed.<ref name="TrueColors">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref>

Many societies in the galaxy had techniques for conceiving artificially rather than organically.<ref name="GG4-1" /> There were clinics where people could conceive a child via a donor,<ref name="LotFR" /> and a few species were unable to reproduce without technology: Bith had completely lost the ability to conceive naturally,<ref name="GG4-1" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> and [[Columi/Legends|Columi]] had lost all predisposition towards physical contact, and reproduction had become a technological process.<ref name="GG4-1" />

==Biological significance==
Most species reached sexual maturity at a certain age; the Ho'Din, for instance, did this around the age of 30.<ref name="GG4-1" /> The [[Jenet/Legends|Jenets]], on the other hand, reached full maturity within one standard year.<ref name="GG4-1" /> This quick rise to self-sufficiency meant that Jenet females were free to bear children relatively often, and the time between litters would seldom exceed a standard year.<ref name="GG4-1" />

Amongst some species, their biology meant that raising and caring for the young was done by a group rather than individual parents. The [[Qieg/Legends|Qieg]] was a sentient [[Insect/Legends|insect]] species, where the females lay eggs that were fertilized by many males. There were no family units, but all the offspring were raised communally. The Qieg did not consider it important to claim offspring as one's own, and made no effort to determine whether a given infant was their child.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> The Ishi Tib of Tibrin had no spouses, and mating was governed by momentary desires on the part of the Ishi Tib.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Ishi Tib would only mate to reproduce.<ref name="Ultimate" /> Once fertilized, the eggs were laid in special hatcheries on the sandbars. The number of eggs allowed to mature was determined by the population requirements of the community, or "school," and the resources of the area where the school lived. The responsibility for raising the young fell to the community as a whole, and no one ever knew which hatchlings came from with parents.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Potential partners were tested to verify that no problems would arise for their offspring.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The [[Rakaan]]s had five life phases which corresponded to unique sexes: Child, neuter, female, male and andro. Each Rakaan would normally experience at least three phases during a lifetime. In the female phase, the Rakaans laid eggs, which were fertilized by the males. The female would then keep the eggs inside her body. After the gestation period was over, the eggs were released into a nesting chamber where the andros cared for the fertilized eggs.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> The [[Lyra]] were [[Cephalopod/Legends|cephalopods]] with a rigid caste system intricately linked to the number of tentacles possessed by the individual Lyra. The fertilized eggs would hatch within a mother's body, upon which she released them into the sea to be cared for by the four-limbed caste.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Verpine hatchlings were cared for by the entire community.<ref name="GG4-1" />

[[Priapulin]] were amphibious gastropods that had a rather bizarre symbiotic<ref name="Essential" /> relationship with small creatures called [[Crast|food-kin]],<ref name="Essential" /> sentient, crab-like beings.<ref name="Rogue Planet">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref> The food-kin provided the Priapulin's nourishment, and were actually proud to fulfill their role as food. Once the Priapulin consumed them, the food-kin's offspring remained inside the Priapulin's body. After a time, the Priapulin gave birth to, and cared for, the food-kin's babies, who in turn would act as food, and so on.<ref name="Essential" /> The Priapulin would have to eat the food-kin when their biological clock chimed, and before their children spoiled.<ref name="Rogue Planet" /> Priapulin [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Charza Kwinn]] even became a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] and a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] in order to feed his food-kin, although he limited his prey to [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperials]].<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

Another species of note were the [[Fefze]]. These [[Arthropod/Legends|arthropods]] resembled [[Beetle/Legends|beetles]], and were one of the rare species with true [[Hive mind/Legends|hive intelligence]]. One of the highest priorities of a Fefze swarm was to recruit new hatchlings in order to spread its mind base and to prolong its life. This was usually accomplished through a "swarm dance," which was a ritualistic gathering in which swarms met for the purpose of reproducing. Males from each swarm fertilized the eggs of females from other swarms. Most of these eggs were brought back to the swarms' home territory of hatching. The two swarms would then work together to form an egg globule belonging to neither of them. This new globule was abandoned in the hope that it would mature into a new swarm. In this manner, the race was perpetuated through the formation of new swarms. The hatchlings from the egg globule, usually coming from a variety of mothers, matured together, playing and feeding as a group, eventually learning how to operate within one mind.<ref name="GG4-1" />

Some species did not consciously decide to reproduce. For example, the [[Pulra]]s, who reproduced through fission, would simply start retaining food energy to nourish a new Pulra growing within their bodies. Natural biochemical fluctuations and subtle levels in the environment would dictate population levels.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> Among the M'shinni, who reproduced through parthenogenesis, reproduction was triggered by climatic conditions; in areas of plentiful food, they would give birth to a single infant once every three standard years.<ref name="GG12" /> The Sekct, who were also parthenogenetic, would lay a single egg every standard two years, although only one in two eggs would hatch, because the species was highly susceptible to random mutations.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> The [[Neti/Legends|Neti]] procreated by creating a few seeds, which occurred only once every few centuries. Seeds would often sit for over a thousand years before germinating.<ref name="Ultimate" /> Sometimes, the new saplings would burst out of the ground after their progenitor's death.<ref name="Dark Empire II 3">[[Dark Empire II 3|''Dark Empire II'' 3]]</ref><ref name="Legacy—War 6">[[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy — War'' 6]]</ref>

Some species also had a natural rhythm that ensured the continuation of the species. Rybet males despised and feared their female counterparts, and the only thing that allowed them to overcome this was the species' overwhelming urge to mate and reproduce, which happened only once every ten years after reaching adulthood.<ref name="Ultimate" /> Rakaans changed sex according to their environment; in times of famine, the neuter population skyrocketed, while in times of severe depopulation, children matured more quickly and the male, female, and andro populations increased at rapid rates.<ref name="Alien Encounters" /> [[Bilar]]s ate and slept in groups in order to survive. Bilars born within a few days of each other developed special affinities and became lifelong members of defensive communities. Within a few generations, the Bilar reproductive circle evolved to maximize each youngling's chance to bond with as many children as possible. Most Bilars were conceived and born within only a few [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] of one or more other Bilars, and small group of expectant mothers would stay close so that the children would be born in physical proximity.<ref name="GG4-1" />
